wars.name: Hephthalite-Kidarite wars

zones.text: Bactria (Tokharistan) and Transoxiana, the Kidarite country

wars.outcome: The Hephthalites beat the Kidarites from the 450s; Peroz I, 'with their help', 'finally vanquished Kidarites in 466' (Kidarites page: Peroz 'reconquering Balkh' in 467); the Hephthalites took Transoxiana about 466 and Sogdia by 479, and the Kidarites withdrew to Gandhara.
wars.note: The Hephthalites page dates the defeat both 450 and 'around 466'; the Peroz I page has the Kidarite war c. 464-466/467 with 'Hephthalite and other Hunnic help'.

wars.name: Peroz I's Hephthalite wars
wars.outcome: Peroz attacked in 474 and was ambushed and captured near Gurgan (ransomed by Zeno); a second campaign in the late 470s or early 480s ended in his capture again and a ransom of silver (his son Kavad hostage in 482); the third, in 484, ended in his death. Nishapur, Herat and Marw passed to the Hephthalites and the Sasanians paid tribute.
wars.note: The pages differ on the 484 battle: the Peroz I page says the site is uncertain ('possibly near Balkh') and has Akhshunwar dig the trench; the Hephthalites page has Peroz 'defeated and killed at the Battle of Herat by Kun-khi'.

wars.name: Kavad I's eastern wars
wars.outcome: Kavad, who had returned in 498/9 with a Hephthalite army, went east against 'hostile Huns' in 503, took the Zundaber castle in 508, and 'by 513 had re-taken the region of Khorasan'.
wars.note: Dates 503, 508 and 513 are the page's; the page says little else about the eastern wars.

wars.name: Hunnic wars (First and Second)
wars.outcome: Toramana reached the maximum extent about 500-515 and was defeated in 515 (Prakashadharma); Mihirakula's Second Hunnic War from 520 ended in defeat in 528 and 'c. 534'; the Punjab and north India were lost by 542.
wars.note: The page treats these as Alchon wars; see the identity note in the 490 ledger event.

wars.name: Göktürk-Sasanian war against the Hephthalites

zones.text: Bactria (Tokharistan) and Transoxiana, the Kidarite country

wars.outcome: The Hephthalite empire was destroyed 'around 560 CE'; the Turks took the land north of the Oxus and the Sasanians held suzerainty south of it.

certainty.note: Steppe and mountain frontiers throughout; no treaty line is dated by the pages. The Sasanian frontier (Khorasan, the Oxus) and the Indian edge are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria row White Huns 410..560 (7 shapes). Corrections: (1) the 410-450 shape is the Xionite/Kidarite land and is dropped; the state starts in 450 on a Kunduz core; (2) the 451 shape holds only from 479, with two new keyframes before it (466-473 without Bactria beyond the Kunduz core and without Sogdia, which the page dates 474 and 479; 474-478 without Sogdia); (3) Khorasan returns to the Sasanians in 513, not 523 (new 513 keyframe). The identity question is not settled: the Alchon Huns page calls the Alchon a separate entity 'now regarded as' distinct from the Hephthalites, while Cliopatria's single row (and the Kidarites page's 'sometimes considered as a branch') draws one empire; the Indian lands (Punjab, Sindh, Gujarat, Kashmir, Gandhara) of the 490-533 shapes and the Kabul fringe are kept here with confidence 1 and flagged. Counterparts needing dossiers: alchon-huns (370-670 on the Alchon infobox), kingdom-of-gaochang (460-640; no longer a counterpart here), and the Hephthalite successors Nezak Huns, Zunbils and the Principality of Chaghaniyan (to 710). The Cliopatria relation '(Alliance between White Huns and Sasanian Empire) 410-489' is partial: the pages have the Hephthalites help Peroz in 458 and against the Kidarites in 466, but fight him in 474-484 and make the Sasanians their tributaries 'from 474 until the middle of the 6th century'. The Sasanian tribute is not recorded as a vassal event (it would tint the whole Sasanian empire). No area figure on any page opened (the Hephthalites page caption 'circa 500' only), so no infobox comparison. Rulers: 'There is no king-list' (Hephthalites page), so no ruler strip; the Alchon page lists Khingila, Mehama, Toramana and Mihirakula, but for the Alchon. Page budget: five pages, all cited. The Hephthalites page puts Peroz's death at the Battle of Herat by Kun-khi, the Peroz I page 'possibly near Balkh'; and the Hephthalites page puts Sogdia both at 479 and 509. Reviewer fixes (second pass): (a) Turfan 479 is demoted from a gain to this note, the reading chosen jointly with rouran-khaganate: only the Hephthalites page says 'In 479 they took the east end of the Tarim Basin, around the region of Turfan' (and 'In 497-509, they pushed north of Turfan to the Urumchi region', 'continued to occupy the Tarim Basin until ... circa 560'); the Gaochang page (Kan Bozhou's 'separate vassal kingdom' of the Rouran from 460, the Gaoche king's vassals from the 480s, the Qu dynasty 501-640 first the Rouran's then the Gaoche's) and the Gaoche page (the Fufuluo 'interfere with the Gaochang' from 481) name no Hephthalites at Turfan, though the Gaoche page has the Hephthalites 'extended their domain to Karashahr' after 492. No White Huns keyframe draws Turfan; the Rouran dossier draws the Gaochang oasis as a vassal tint 460-481 and Hami as Rouran land. If a gap-filler prefers the Hephthalite reading it must remove Turfan-Hami from the Rouran keyframes of 481-554 and add it here from 479 to 560. (b) Sogdia (479) no longer names the Kidarites as counterpart (kidarites.json ends in 467) and is no longer in the 466 gain. (c) Bactria beyond the Kunduz core is drawn Sasanian 466-473. Thin items re-examined (second pass): the Indian lands of 490 stay Cliopatria's and Alchon on the pages (Toramana page: Alchon; Hephthalites page: 'never went beyond the Hindu-Kush'); the 534 loss stays to nobody (Yashodharman page names no heir polity); the 560 handover of Kabulistan to the Turk Shahis is contradicted by the Turk Shahis page (established 665, replacing the Nezak Huns), so sa-03 should decide the row's real start; the south-of-Oxus remainder is still unallocated (Khosrow I page: the Oxus frontier and Chaghaniyan as a Sasanian vassal, no year). [fx-23, 2026-11-01] Conflict with alchon-huns settled in favour of the Alchon dossier: every keyframe from 451 on subtracts the Alchon country south of the Hindu Kush (Hephthalites page: the Hephthalites 'never went beyond the Hindu-Kush, which was occupied by the Alchon Huns'; Alchon Huns page: a separate entity holding Kabulistan, Gandhara, the Punjab, Malwa, Gujarat, Kashmir, Sindh); the 490 gain 'from alchon-huns' is rewritten; the 496-534 contest with the Gupta over Malwa and the Punjab is removed (the alchon-huns dossier has the Hunnic wars); the 451 and 490 keyframes now carry the years their text always gave (479-489, 490-512); the found of 450 names alchon-huns as counterpart.
